headline: US stocks ended mixed as global bond selloff pushed Treasury yields toward multi-decade highs and Brent crude held above $100 on Middle East tensions
raw_text:
- The Dow Jones Industrial Average ($DJI) fell 160 points to close near 51,380, the S&P 500 ($SPX) finished around 7,703, and the Nasdaq Composite ($COMP) ended nearly flat after paring earlier losses
- The 30-year Treasury yield hit its highest level since 2004 and the 10-year approached 5.2%, extending a third straight day of equity pressure amid a global bond selloff
- Brent crude (@QA) traded above $100 per barrel on Middle East tensions, while reports of U.S.–Iran talks on the Strait of Hormuz helped ease some oil-related anxiety
- Energy shares outperformed on higher oil prices, while technology lagged as Oracle (ORCL) slid about 4% after issuing a force majeure notice tied to its Project Jupiter New Mexico data center
- Everpure Inc. (P) jumped about 11% after issuing a preliminary fiscal 2028 revenue outlook of $7–7.3 billion, implying 39–45% growth and topping consensus, alongside a non-GAAP operating income target of $1.7–1.9 billion
- Meta Platforms (META) gained 3.7% after its Connect event unveiled the Muse handheld AI device, new VR goggles, and smart glasses
- McDonald’s (MCD) shares declined after BMO, Evercore ISI and TD Cowen cut price targets following its NEXT strategy investor day
- MGM Resorts (MGM) fell after People Incorporated withdrew its $18 billion buyout proposal
- Darden Restaurants (DRI) reported first-quarter EPS of $2.05 on $3.2 billion in revenue, in line with estimates, with same-restaurant sales up 3.1%
- Costco Wholesale (COST) reported after the bell with an initially muted after-hours reaction as investors looked ahead to progress on Trump–Xi talks and the next wave of earnings
